newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia cuts military budget in austerity drive.
newsitem.headline: Colombia cuts military budget in austerity drive.

text.p: Colombia, bogged down in Latin America's longest guerrilla war, is to slice more than $120 million from its military budget in a government austerity drive, Defence Minister Guillermo Alberto Gonzalez said on Tuesday.

About half the cuts will be borne by the army, which is already complaining that it does not have sufficient funds to combat leftist rebels embarked on one of their bloodiest offensives in three decades.
Some of the budget reductions will inevitably fall on the police force, which with the army plays a lead role in the fight against drug trafficking.

But Gonzalez promised the army's on-going counterinsurgency campaign would not suffer. He said the basic defence budget will be slashed back to about $300 million but will receive a cash injection from the sale of "war bonds" to rich Colombians that could net up to an additional $600 million.

"The armed forces budget is being cut as part of the overall fiscal adjustment. We cannot act like a loose cannon and must bear our share of the burden," he told reporters. "But funding for the creation of new batallions and the provision of new equipment has different origins such as war bonds."

Even with the cuts, Colombia's total defence expenditure for 1997, including war bonds, is expected to be between $800 million and $900 million, about three percent of the overall budget. It equals the combined military spending of the last four years.
The budget cuts come against the backdrop of the government's efforts to rein in a burgeoning fiscal deficit.
